title: Officers Surround Armed Homicide Suspect Then Gunfire Breaks Out
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Louisville, Kentucky — On March 20, 2026, officers responded to a shooting on East Caldwell Street. Inside a residence, they found two men suffering from gunshot wounds. One victim, Remon Allen, was pronounced dead at the scene, while Rayvon Allen, his twin brother survived after being transported to the hospital. Following an extensive investigation, detectives identified 18-year-old Nathan Walker as the primary suspect in the homicide and assault. Over the following weeks, officers worked to locate Walker. On April 6, 2026, detectives received a tip that he was in the downtown area near a Taco Bell at First and Broadway. Officers moved into the area to find him and, after positively identifying him in the parking lot, coordinated a plan to approach and detain him. As officers approached and began issuing commands for Walker to put his hands on his head, he quickly produced a handgun and pointed it at officers, prompting an exchange of gunfire within seconds. Authorities said Walker continued to pose a threat even after being struck, at one point attempting to raise his weapon again as officers repeatedly ordered him to drop it. Multiple officers fired during the encounter as the situation escalated in what police described as an immediate threat to officer and public safety. Walker was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators later confirmed he had discharged a firearm during the incident and was in possession of two guns, including one believed to have been used in the earlier homicide. The shooting remains under investigation and will undergo multiple levels of review.
